title: Fold — ideas with room to unfold
author: Smithright Tools

slides.title:
Make the point.
Leave room
to explore.
slides.body:
A presentation for the room.
A document for the curious.
slides.label: FOLD / OPEN PRESENTATION TEMPLATE

items.label: Make it yours
items.text: Edit, reorder, and take it with you.

details.title: The fold is a promise
details.body: The first screen carries the argument. Evidence, explanation, and references live below it. A reader can go deeper without forcing a presenter to put everything on the screen.

details.title: Try this
details.body: Use the arrows to explore the examples. Choose Read to see the full document, or Edit to change the deck. Everything here works without a connection. The examples contain illustrative content, not measured product results.

slides.notes: Open with the distinction between a clear argument and the material that supports it.

slides.title:
Make the structure
visible.
slides.body:
Clean geometry. Named components.
A system you can explain at a glance.
slides.label: REFERENCE ARCHITECTURE / ILLUSTRATIVE

details.title: An editable drawing
details.body: Every connector, node, and annotation is native SVG. Text remains text, lines remain crisp, and the diagram has an accessible description. Change the item labels in the editor or JSON to adapt the architecture.

details.title: Design principle
details.body: Use position and connection to explain the relationship. Reserve color for emphasis. Avoid making a diagram depend on motion or color alone.

slides.notes: Walk from intent through the controlled execution path to evidence.

slides.title:
Show the loop.
Not just the boxes.
slides.body:
A living system senses, decides, acts,
and learns from what actually happened.
slides.label: CONCEPTUAL FLOW / NOT LIVE TELEMETRY

details.title: Motion with a job
details.body: The traveling markers communicate direction and recurrence. Pause the motion to inspect the structure. Reduced-motion preferences are honored, and PDF output keeps the full static diagram.

details.title: An honest animation
details.body: This is an explanatory animation. It is not connected to a service and does not claim that a real operation ran. Replace the labels to use the loop for product delivery, scientific experiments, or operational recovery.

slides.notes: Pause the animation when discussing an individual stage.

slides.title:
Give abstract ideas
a place to live.
slides.body:
An illustrated landscape of people,
platforms, and possibilities.
slides.label: ORIGINAL VECTOR SCENE / NO IMAGE DEPENDENCIES

details.title: Dimension as a visual language
details.body: Isometric projection gives a family of icons a shared perspective. Here, the buildings, layers, paths, and light source are drawn with SVG. There are no stock assets, remote fonts, or raster textures to retrieve.

details.title: Use it intentionally
details.body: This style works for platform maps, product ecosystems, and journeys. For a quantitative comparison, use the chart example instead: decorative depth should never distort a measurement.

slides.notes: Use the scene as an overview, then move to specific relationships.

slides.title:
Beyond the
known horizon.
slides.body: Build a world worth stepping into.
slides.label: CHAPTER ONE / THE NEXT FRONTIER

details.title: Game-studio art direction
details.body: A restrained interface sits over an original vector environment: distant planet, layered terrain, atmospheric light, and a small human silhouette for scale. The composition borrows the discipline of cinematic title screens without copying a game or studio identity.

details.title: Built to travel
details.body: The entire scene is SVG. It renders locally, remains sharp in print, and needs no downloaded art. The accent color controls the planet glow and the chapter marker.

slides.notes: Give this slide a moment of silence before introducing the next chapter.

slides.title:
Let the evidence
do the talking.
slides.body:
A clear comparison beats
a crowded dashboard.
slides.label: ILLUSTRATIVE DATA / NOT A PERFORMANCE CLAIM

details.title: Read the scale
details.body: The example compares three illustrative scores on a fixed 0–100 scale. Values are printed beside the bars, so color is not required to understand the chart. Edit the values in the slide content; bars and labels update together.

details.title: Supply the source
details.body: For a real presentation, replace this text with the source, date, sample, measurement method, and uncertainty. Keep a comparison honest by using the same denominator and reporting meaningful limitations.

slides.notes: These are demonstration values. Do not present them as actual results.

slides.title:
Your ideas.
Your rhythm.
Your next move.
slides.body:
Start with a point of view.
Make the template your own.
slides.label: OPEN A DECK. CHANGE THE ORDER. TELL YOUR STORY.

details.title: A small creative instrument
details.body: A single portable HTML file holds the presentation, its content, and the editor. JSON provides an uncomplicated authoring contract for people and agents. Stable IDs make precise changes possible without relying on slide numbers.

details.title: Share the result
details.body: Download HTML to share a runnable deck, or JSON to keep editable source. Print slides alone or include the details. A hosted editor changes your local draft; publishing still requires updating the hosted file.

slides.notes: Invite the audience to try editing and exporting their own version.
